doctor_notes: Fever for 5 days, rising each evening, 39.4°C. Coated tongue, mild tender splenomegaly. Widal and blood culture sent. Started oral cefixime 200 mg BD for 14 days, paracetamol SOS. Review in 5 days or earlier if worse.

diagnosis: Enteric fever – not responding to oral cefixime
doctor_notes: Day 6 of cefixime. Still febrile, 39.0°C, appetite poor. Blood culture: Salmonella Typhi, SENSITIVE to cefixime and ceftriaxone. Patient and wife confirm every dose taken; strips shown. Poor response despite a sensitive organism – cause unclear. Admit for IV ceftriaxone.
Admitted. IV ceftriaxone 2 g OD started. Oral cefixime stopped. Hydration and antipyretics.
Afebrile 72 h after starting IV ceftriaxone. Eating well. Discharged to complete 10 days of therapy. Note: rapid response to IV drug after 6 days of no response to oral cefixime.
HbA1c 7.4%. Fasting lipids: LDL 172 mg/dL, TG 310 mg/dL, HDL 38. Started rosuvastatin 20 mg + fenofibrate 160 mg (Rosuvas F 20) at night. Diet counselling. Repeat lipid profile in 3 months.
Refill. Taking Rosuvas F 20 nightly. No muscle pain. Continue.
Refill. Good adherence by pill count. Continue.

3-month lipids: LDL 158, TG 305, HDL 37. Almost no change in triglycerides on fenofibrate. Pill count matches, diet followed. Unusual non-response. Plan: continue, recheck in 8 weeks; consider omega-3 or a dose change.
Refill. No new complaints.

diagnosis: Mixed dyslipidaemia – not at target after 5 months
doctor_notes: Lipids: LDL 161, TG 318. Still far from target after 5 months of daily therapy. Added ezetimibe 10 mg. Considering rosuvastatin 40 mg – needs review of why the current drug is not working.
6 weeks after delivery. Hb 7.9 g/dL, ferritin 6 ng/mL. Could not tolerate oral iron (vomiting). Plan IV iron sucrose 200 mg on alternate days, 5 doses, in day care.

diagnosis: IV iron – reaction after first dose
doctor_notes: Iron sucrose 200 mg in 100 ml NS over 30 min. About 2 h later: fever 38.9°C with chills and rigors. Cannula site red, warm and tender. Infusion line removed, blood culture sent, paracetamol given. Kept for observation.
Blood culture: coagulase-negative staphylococci, 1 of 2 bottles – contaminant vs true infection unclear. Thrombophlebitis at cannula site. Started oral antibiotic. Remaining iron doses postponed.
Afebrile, cannula site healed. Hb 8.6 g/dL. IV iron to resume – needs review before the next dose.
BP 162/98 (average of 3). ECG normal, creatinine 0.9, potassium normal. Started telmisartan 40 mg OD. Home BP diary advised.
BP 158/96. Home readings similar. Takes the tablet every morning. Low-salt diet reinforced. Continue telmisartan 40 mg.
BP 156/94 after 2 months of telmisartan. Response much weaker than expected for this dose. Adherence confirmed. Added amlodipine 5 mg OD.
BP 150/92. Partial response to the second drug only. Plan to increase telmisartan to 80 mg – needs review.
Worry, poor sleep for 4 months. Started sertraline 25 mg OD and short-term lorazepam 1 mg at bedtime. Review in 4 weeks.
Still sleeping only 3–4 h. Takes lorazepam every night with no clear effect. Increased lorazepam to 2 mg at bedtime. Fall-risk advice given.
Sleep slightly better on 2 mg. Continue lorazepam 2 mg at bedtime; plan slow taper later.
Refill. Same dose. No daytime drowsiness.
Refill. Same dose. Stable.
Refill. Pharmacy now supplies a different brand of lorazepam 1 mg. Same dose of 2 mg at bedtime.

diagnosis: Fall at home with excessive drowsiness
doctor_notes: Brought by daughter. 1 week of heavy daytime drowsiness and unsteady walking since the new strip was started; fell in the bathroom. Bruise on left hip, X-ray: no fracture. Dose unchanged at 2 mg for 6 months. Lorazepam withheld tonight. Psychiatry review – needs review of the dose.
